title: How many species are there?
sub: Symposium topic 6 · Mora et al. 2011 vs Wiens 2023
blurb: Species concepts, cryptic diversity, extrapolation and why 8.7 million may be far too low.
h1: How many species are on Earth, and why is it hard to say?
lede: Group 6's question. Classic: Mora et al. (2011), who estimated about 8.7 million species by extrapolating from higher taxa. Recent: Wiens (2023), progress and problems.
six: **Species concepts**: biological (interbreeding, reproductively isolated), morphological (distinct looks), phylogenetic (smallest diagnosable lineage). Different concepts give different counts.
The **biological species concept** (Mayr) fails for asexual organisms and prokaryotes, geographic isolation and hybridisation.
**Mora et al. 2011**: extrapolated from higher taxa (regression) → about **8.75 million** species.
**Cryptic diversity**: lookalike species lumped under one name (e.g. African savanna vs forest elephant).
Wiens 2023 problems: limited DNA data, cryptic diversity, underestimated **prokaryotes**, and Mora's wrong **assumption of stagnation** (>700 new genera are described each year).
**Extrapolation** = estimating total richness beyond what was sampled.
must: species concepts and why estimates differ
foot: Source: Group 6 symposium slides and notes; glossary section 6 f–h.

questions.q: The biological species concept defines a species as…
questions.answer: Interbreeding natural populations reproductively isolated from others

questions.q: For which organisms does the biological species concept fail?
questions.e: Also problems with geographic isolation and hybridisation.

questions.q: A horse and a donkey produce a mule. Why are they still separate species?
questions.e: Biological concept: the offspring must also be able to reproduce.

questions.q: Roughly how many species did Mora et al. 2011 estimate?
questions.e: 8.75 million, by extrapolating from higher taxa.

questions.q: How did Mora et al. reach their estimate?
questions.answer: Extrapolating from the numbers of higher taxa with a regression
questions.e: They assumed higher taxa had levelled off (stagnated).

questions.answer: Distinct, reproductively isolated lineages lumped under one name because they look alike
questions.e: E.g. Loxodonta africana and L. cyclotis.

questions.q: Which assumption of Mora et al. did Wiens criticise as 'stagnation'?
questions.answer: That higher taxa have stopped growing
questions.e: Over 700 new genera are described each year.

questions.q: Which group does Wiens think may be a major driver of Earth's species richness?
Using sampled data to estimate total richness beyond what was sampled is called…
Robert May's estimate (10–50 million animals) came from which method?
questions.e: Limitation: species don't follow one scaling law.

questions.q: Why count species at all, according to Group 6?
questions.answer: To find threatened species, calculate extinction rates and track climate change
wrong: Because laws require a fixed number

questions.q: What did Mora et al. say would be needed to describe all species?

vocab.meaning: A framework for defining what counts as a species.
Interbreeding populations reproductively isolated from others (Mayr).
Two species interbreeding (common in plants, some ducks).
Distinct lineages lumped under one name because they look alike.
Estimating total richness beyond the sampled range.
Ranks above species: genus, family, order, class, phylum.
Operational taxonomic unit: a DNA-based group used in place of species for microbes.
Identifying many species at once from DNA in a sample.

facts: The biological species concept was defined by Ernst {Mayr|Darwin|Linnaeus|Wallace}.
The biological species concept fails for {asexual|large|marine|rare} organisms.
Mora et al. 2011 estimated about {8.7|1.2|50|100} million species.
Lookalike species lumped under one name are cryptic {diversity|species pairs|hybrids|clades}.
More than {700|7|70000|70} new genera are described each year.
